chunks: He said: Abu Nasr Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Muqri al-Baseer reported to me from Abdullah ibn Yahya al-Qattan, who reported from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Sa’id al-Qurashi, who reported from his father, who reported from al-Husayn ibn Mukhariq, from Abdul Samad ibn Ali, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Abbas — may God be pleased with him — who said:

When the Messenger of God, peace be upon him and his family, passed away, the Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him, undertook his ritual washing, with al-Abbas and al-Fadl ibn al-Abbas assisting him. When Ali, peace be upon him, finished washing him, he removed the wrap-cloth from his face and said:

“May my father and mother be your ransom. You were pure in life and pure in death. With your passing, there has been severed what was never severed by the death of anyone else: prophethood and divine revelation. You were so distinguished that your death became a source of consolation for all other bereavements, and you were so universal that all people grieve equally for you. Had you not commanded patience and forbidden restless grief, we would have shed incessant tears over you. But deep sorrow and choking grief are two inseparable companions — they are an affliction of fate, and yet they are too trivial for you. May my father and mother be your ransom, remember us in the presence of your Lord, and keep us in your concern.”
Then he leaned over him, kissed his face, and drew the cloth over him.

key_terms.غسل: Ghusl — the ritual washing of the deceased

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say when washing the body of Prophet Muhammad after his death?
ai.summary: This narration describes the deeply moving scene following the Prophet Muhammad’s death, as Imam Ali (AS) performed the ritual washing of his body. Ali’s eulogy, delivered in the presence of al-Abbas and al-Fadl ibn al-Abbas, is one of the most eloquent expressions of grief in Islamic literature, acknowledging the finality of prophethood and the universal loss suffered by all humanity.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 4. He said: Abu Nasr Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Muqri al-Baseer reported to me from Abdullah ibn Yahya al-Qattan, who reported from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Saeed al-Qarshi, who reported from his father, who reported from al-Husayn ibn Mukhariq, from Abdul Samad ibn ‘Ali, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Abbas - may Allah be pleased with him, who said:

When the Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, passed away, Amirul Mu’mineen ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib, together with al-Abbas and al-Fadhl ibn al-Abbas, washed him. And when they had finished washing him, he (‘Ali) removed the wrap-cloth from his face and said:

"My father and my mother be your ransom, you have been pure in your life and in your death. With your passing away, there has been a cessation, which has no parallel in anyone else’s death; the cessation of Prophethood and the Divine revelations. You are so exalted that, your death has become a source of solace and consolation for all other bereavements and (at the same time) your death has such a common aspect, that all men all equally grieved by it. And, had it not been that you ordered forbearance and forbade restless grief, we would have shed incessant tears over you. (But deep sorrow and grief, both are too trivial to give any consolation on your parting). May my father and my mother be your ransom, do remember us (well) when you are in the presence of your Sustainer, and keep us in your mind."
Then he fell over him, kissed his face and drew the cloth over him.
